To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel convolutional network architecture that can be trained to detect and segment the left ventricular myocardium and the 4 cardiac chambers simultaneously, without requiring prior knowledge of the clinical view.

we developed a novel CNN architecture for simultaneous detection and segmentation of multiple classes, that we demonstrated the efficacy of this architecture on a challenging segmentation problem, and that we showed that this architecture outperformed prior approaches.

a new deep learning architecture called \Omega} Net was developed for simultaneous detection, orientation prediction, and semantic segmentation in 2 D cardiac MRI, and that \Omega} Nets outperformed U Nets on the task of cardiac MRI segmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of deep learning architectures to solve challenging problems in cardiac imaging.
developing deep learning methods to improve the detection, orientation, and segmentation of cardiac MR images.
the development of a novel CNN architecture for the simultaneous detection, orientation, and segmentation of the heart in 2 D SSFP cine sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Omega Net architecture represents a substantial advancement over previous work on cardiac image segmentation, and that this architecture has broad implications for biomedical image analysis more generally.
the Omega Net architecture is a novel convolutional network architecture for simultaneous detection and semantic segmentation of cardiac structures from 2 D cine MR images.
the proposed architecture, Omega Net, outperformed prior state of the art methods on the task of simultaneous detection, orientation prediction, and segmentation of cardiac MRI images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented an end to end deep learning architecture for simultaneous cardiac detection, orientation, and segmentation.
we have developed a novel CNN architecture for simultaneous detection and segmentation that is robust to variations in appearance, contrast, orientation, and position.
we present a novel CNN architecture that is capable of simultaneously detecting, transforming into a canonical view, and segmenting the heart in 2D SSFP cine sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
detection, orientation and segmentation should be jointly performed in a single network.
by combining detection, orientation, and segmentation in a single network, we can improve segmentation performance.
by incorporating the detection of the object of interest and the orientation estimation of the object of interests, we can achieve better performance in semantic segmentation.
